personas.name: The bank-branch fund holder
personas.who: A beginner whose money sits in mutual funds bought through a bank advisor, who has just noticed the yearly fee.
fears: paying for advice that doesn't hold up
an advisor who gets a commission on the fund he sells
wants: to know what MER is acceptable
a straight answer on whether to trust the bank advisor
one simple low cost fund instead of a confusing mix
words: unlikely to be worth the 1% premium
He gets a commission on the 1.73% MER
low cost globally diversified index fund
personas.stops_for: A real fee number like 2.66% next to what that fee costs in dollars over the years.
personas.saves: A side-by-side of a bank fund's MER and a one-fund ETF's MER, plus the questions to ask the advisor.

personas.name: The late starter with unused room
personas.who: Someone just getting started, with cash sitting in chequing and TFSA, RRSP or FHSA room they haven't used or can't work out.
fears: cash that's losing a good amount to inflation
a CRA penalty for putting in too much
wants: to know how much TFSA room they actually have
to know whether a big goal like $3.7M is normal
a better place for the emergency fund than chequing
the exact dates for new room and deadlines
words: Just getting started at 35. Am I too late?
I need 3.7 million to live comfortably?
Is this way correct for calculating TFSA contribution room
lost a good amount due to inflation
personas.stops_for: A dollar figure showing what waiting one more year costs, or how much room has piled up since 2009.
personas.saves: A dated checklist with the TFSA limit announcement, the March 1 RRSP deadline and how to check their room.

personas.name: The headline-chasing new holder
personas.who: A new holder of bitcoin, a bitcoin ETF or hot AI and single-stock products who is now down after this fall's drops.
fears: coins stuck on an exchange that got hacked
a 20% drop from one earnings report
not knowing whether to sell, hold or keep buying
wants: to know if money frozen on a platform comes back
to know the year-end tax-loss cutoff
to know what they're actually buying behind a famous ticker
words: Hackers stole $6 billion in digital coins from Binance
Crypto slides after record Binance hack
that defeats the purpose of having a set allocation
personas.stops_for: A big fresh loss number from the news, like the $6.3B hack or a 34.86% loss on a high-yield ETF, with a plain answer to whether their own money is safe.
personas.saves: A year-end crypto checklist covering the tax-loss cutoff, the 30-day superficial loss rule and the records to keep before CARF reporting.
